chapter.chapter_title: The present tense of -ir and -re verbs

attestations.source_text: Type 1 verbs drop the -ir of the infinitive, add an -iss- to the plural form, and then insert the appropriate ending.
Type 2 -ir verbs drop the -ir of the infinitive, then add the appropriate ending, without the -iss- in the nous and vous forms.

concepts.name: Present tense
concepts.description: The present tense of French verbs, including -ir, -re, and previously studied -er verbs.

attestations.source_text: The present tense of -ir and -re verbs

concepts.name: -ir verbs
concepts.description: Verbs ending in -ir in the infinitive, which follow two conjugation patterns: Type 1 (with -iss- infix) and Type 2 (irregular).

concepts.name: -re verbs
concepts.description: Verbs ending in -re in the infinitive, which follow a regular pattern or are irregular (prendre group).

concepts.name: Regular conjugation
concepts.description: Conjugation patterns that follow predictable rules, such as Type 1 -ir verbs and regular -re verbs.

attestations.source_text: Type 1 verbs drop the -ir of the infinitive, add an -iss- to the plural form, and then insert the appropriate ending.

concepts.name: Irregular conjugation
concepts.description: Conjugation patterns that do not follow predictable rules, such as Type 2 -ir verbs and irregular -re verbs (prendre group).

attestations.source_text: These groups of -ir verbs can be termed irregular.

concepts.name: Interrogation
concepts.description: Ways of forming questions in French: inversion, est-ce que, and intonation.

attestations.source_text: In French there are three ways of asking questions.

concepts.name: Negation
concepts.description: Ways of making sentences negative, including ne...pas, other negative particles, and ni...ni...

attestations.source_text: To make a sentence negative, you simply place ne... pas around the verb.

concepts.name: Languages
concepts.description: Vocabulary for languages (German, English, Arabic, etc.) introduced in the chapter.

grammar_rules.summary: Drop -ir, add -iss- to plural forms, then add appropriate endings.
grammar_rules.explanation: For Type 1 -ir verbs, remove the -ir ending from the infinitive. In the plural forms (nous, vous, ils/elles), add -iss- before the ending. The endings are: je -is, tu -is, il -it, nous -issons, vous -issez, ils -issent.
usage: Present tense conjugation of regular -ir verbs
conditions: Verbs ending in -ir that follow this pattern
common_traps: Do not forget the -iss- in plural forms.

attestations.source_text: Type 1 verbs drop the -ir of the infinitive, add an -iss- to the plural form, and then insert the appropriate ending.

grammar_rules.explanation: For Type 2 -ir verbs, remove the -ir ending and add the appropriate endings directly, without inserting -iss-. These verbs are irregular. Example: sortir -> je sors, tu sors, il sort, nous sortons, vous sortez, ils sortent.
usage: Present tense conjugation of irregular -ir verbs
conditions: Verbs ending in -ir that do not take -iss-
common_traps: Do not add -iss- in nous and vous forms.

attestations.source_text: Type 2 -ir verbs drop the -ir of the infinitive, then add the appropriate ending, without the -iss- in the nous and vous forms.

grammar_rules.explanation: For regular -re verbs, remove the -re ending and add: je -s, tu -s, il/elle - (no ending), nous -ons, vous -ez, ils/elles -ent. Example: vendre -> je vends, tu vends, il vend, nous vendons, vous vendez, ils vendent.
usage: Present tense conjugation of regular -re verbs
conditions: Verbs ending in -re that follow this pattern
common_traps: The third person singular (il/elle) has no ending.

attestations.source_text: For regular -re verbs, remove the -re ending and follow the pattern below.

grammar_rules.summary: Prendre and its derivatives have irregular pattern: je prends, nous prenons, etc.
grammar_rules.explanation: Some -re verbs are irregular. Prendre conjugates as: je prends, tu prends, il prend, nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent. Variations (apprendre, comprendre, entreprendre, surprendre) follow the same pattern with prefixes.
usage: Present tense conjugation of irregular -re verbs
common_traps: Do not forget the double n in plural forms (nous prenons, vous prenez, ils prennent).

attestations.source_text: Some fairly common -re verbs are irregular. Let’s look at prendre (to take):

grammar_rules.summary: Invert subject and verb to form a question.
grammar_rules.explanation: Form questions by inverting the subject and verb. Example: Comprenez-vous la question? If the third-person singular verb ends with a vowel, insert -t- between verb and pronoun for pronunciation: Parle-t-elle russe?
grammar_rules.formation: verb + hyphen + subject pronoun (+ -t- if necessary)
exceptions: -t- insertion after vowel in third person singular
common_traps: Do not forget the hyphen; remember -t- insertion.

attestations.source_text: You can do an inversion of the subject and the verb... If the third-person singular of a verb ends with a vowel, a -t- is inserted to facilitate the pronunciation.

grammar_rules.summary: Use est-ce que before subject + verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: Place est-ce que before the subject and verb to form a question. Est-ce que becomes est-ce qu' before a vowel. Example: Est-ce que vous habitez à New York? Est-ce qu'ils vendent des timbres?
grammar_rules.negative_form: est-ce que + subject + ne + verb + pas
common_traps: Do not forget the hyphen in est-ce que; use est-ce qu' before vowel.

attestations.source_text: A more colloquial way of asking a question is to use the est-ce que form in front of the subject + verb.

grammar_rules.summary: Keep subject + verb order and raise intonation.
grammar_rules.explanation: Form a question by keeping the affirmative word order (subject + verb) and using an upward intonation at the end of the sentence. Example: Tu finis à cinq heures?
common_traps: Intonation is essential; otherwise it's a statement.

attestations.source_text: A third way of asking a question, colloquially, is keeping the order subject + verb and speaking with an upward intonation.

grammar_rules.summary: Place ne...pas around the conjugated verb.
grammar_rules.explanation: To make a sentence negative, place ne before the conjugated verb and pas after it. If the verb starts with a vowel or mute h, ne becomes n'. Examples: Elle ne travaille pas le lundi. Je n'habite pas à Strasbourg.
exceptions: ne becomes n' before vowel or mute h
common_traps: Do not forget the ne, even in spoken French; remember elision.

attestations.source_text: To make a sentence negative, you simply place ne... pas around the verb.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Other negations (personne, jamais, plus, rien, guère)
grammar_rules.summary: Use ne...personne, ne...jamais, ne...plus, ne...rien, ne...guère.
grammar_rules.explanation: In addition to ne...pas, other negative particles can be used in the same construction: ne...personne (nobody), ne...jamais (never), ne...plus (no longer), ne...rien (nothing), ne...guère (hardly). Examples: Il n'attend personne. Tu ne voyages jamais en hiver. Il n'a plus de patience. Elle ne répond rien. Ce n'est guère raisonnable.
common_traps: Do not confuse plus (no longer) with plus (more); note guère is formal.

attestations.source_text: Aside from ne... pas, there are other negations, constructed in the same way.

grammar_rules.summary: ni...ni... negates two nouns; ne before verb; articles behave differently.
grammar_rules.explanation: The negation ni...ni... precedes each noun it negates, and ne (n') comes before the verb. If a definite article (le, la, l', les) is used before the nouns in the affirmative, it remains in the negative. If an indefinite or partitive article is used, it disappears in the negative. Examples: Il n'aime ni le café ni le chocolat. Elle ne commande ni eau ni vin.
grammar_rules.formation: ne + verb + ni + noun1 + ni + noun2
grammar_rules.word_order: ne + verb + ni + noun + ni + noun
common_traps: Remember definite articles stay; indefinite/partitive articles disappear.

attestations.source_text: The negation ni… ni… precedes each noun that it negates.

exceptions_and_traps.title: -t- insertion in third person singular inversion
exceptions_and_traps.description: When forming a question by inversion with a third-person singular subject pronoun and a verb ending in a vowel, a -t- is inserted between the verb and the pronoun for pronunciation.

attestations.source_text: If the third-person singular of a verb ends with a vowel, a -t- is inserted to facilitate the pronunciation.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Article retention/dropping with ni...ni...
exceptions_and_traps.description: With ni...ni..., definite articles are retained, but indefinite and partitive articles are dropped.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Il n'aime ni le café ni le chocolat. / Elle ne commande ni eau ni vin.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Il n'aime ni café ni chocolat. / Elle ne commande ni de l'eau ni du vin.

attestations.source_text: When the definite article le, la, l’, les is used before the noun, the definite article remains... When the indefinite or partitive article is used... the article disappears.

exceptions_and_traps.description: Type 2 -ir verbs do not take the -iss- infix in plural forms, unlike Type 1 -ir verbs.
